data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Doniel means 'My people are God'. It is a name of biblical origin, most notably given to Daniel, who is known for his unwavering faith in God despite living in exile in Babylon. The name Doniel carries the meaning “My people are God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Doniel usually hope their child will grow to embody my people are god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Doniel carries a rich cultural significance, particularly within the Christian community. It symbolizes an unwavering commitment to God, even in the face of adversity or change. Through the story of Daniel in the Old Testament, the name Doniel is associated with strength and resilience, as Daniel remained true to his faith while navigating the complexities of life in a foreign land.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Doniel emphasizes the importance of keeping our focus on God, no matter where we are in life or what challenges we may face. It serves as a reminder that our connection to God is an essential aspect of our identity and can give us the strength and courage to persevere. The name inspires us to trust in God and to prioritize our relationship with Him above all else.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Doniel is believed to derive from the Hebrew name Dani'el, meaning "God is my judge." It symbolizes faith in God's justice and fairness, and trust in His ultimate judgment. The spiritual meaning is a reminder to live in accordance with God's laws and seek His guidance, knowing that He will bring about righteousness and justice in His divine timing.

biblical_reference.note: Not a direct biblical name, but a variant of Daniel

historical_references.reference: In the Old Testament book of Daniel, the Hebrew name Dani'el (Hebrew: דָּנִיאֵל) is transliterated as Doniel in some versions. Daniel was a Hebrew prophet during the Babylonian exile (6th century BCE) and was renowned for his wisdom and faithfulness to God.

The name Doniel appears in the 12th century CE in the French epic poem 'The Song of Roland.' In this work, Doniel is the name of Roland's nephew and ally who fights alongside him during the Battle of Roncevaux.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Doniel' has gained popularity in modern times as a unique and uncommon name, especially among younger generations. It has been seen on various social media platforms, most notably TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube Gaming. On TikTok, users have created content featuring the name 'Doniel' in various contexts, from music videos to comedy skits. On Instagram, it has been used as a username or handle for various accounts, showcasing a range of interests from fitness and fashion to art and travel. In the gaming community on YouTube, 'Doniel' has been used as a username for competitive gamers, showcasing their skills and strategies to a large audience. As a whole, the name 'Doniel' represents a modern, unique identity that transcends traditional societal norms and is embraced by a diverse range of individuals across various platforms and communities.
